 "content": "# Continual-ARC task-d06d6d7f — solved

## Input/demo and exact rule
The task shows a noisy grid containing large rectangular color panels among background-colored cells. Markers are isolated single cells with colors such as 4/7/8/0 embedded in or near objects. The demonstration's output cleans away those marker/noise cells and preserves the underlying solid rectangles and background. In the test (19x12, background 9), remove the single 4 at row 12, column 12, leaving background 9; remove the 7 at row 15, column 11, restoring background 9; remove the 4s at row 18 column 3 and row 19 column 5, restoring the rectangle color 6. All other cells remain unchanged. Rows/columns here are 1-indexed.

Test objects: 6 rectangle rows 3-4 cols 2-7; 8 rectangle rows 7-9 cols 2-5; 0 rectangle rows 6-12 cols 7-10; lower 6 patches rows 14-19 cols 3-6 and rows 14-17 cols 9-10. Correct output was original grid with the four marker cells replaced by their locally consistent object's color/background as above. Solved after one incorrect submission.

## Demonstration-derived approach
Demo input had marker cells 0/4/8 embedded on otherwise uniform blocks/background. Output removed the markers, filling them with the surrounding uniform object color (e.g. 8 inside color-9/background panels became 9; 4 or 0 inside color-7 patches became 7; marker 8 in color-2 patch became 2; markers 4/0 in background 1 became 1). It also leaves all solid colored rectangles and background unchanged. Therefore treat isolated anomalous marker cells as noise and replace from their containing region's uniform color, not by globally mapping marker colors. In the test the two markers inside color-6 region become 6; markers outside objects become background 9.

Avoid premature speculative submissions: the first wrong guess preserved all blocks and changed only the background marker, missing the other three anomalous cells. Compare every singleton marker against the locally uniform region and update each one. The final correct output is evidence for this pattern, though this is one task instance."
